learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how businesses scale up through franchising, mergers, acquisitions, and creating powerful market synergies!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Internal expansion means growing from within (adding new products, increasing capacity). External expansion means growing by joining with other businesses (Mergers, Acquisitions, Franchising).

An arrangement where one party (Franchisor) grants another party (Franchisee) the right to use its trademark or trade-name as well as certain business systems and processes, to produce and market a good or service.
A combination of two companies into one larger company. Usually, two companies of similar size agree to go forward as a single new company rather than remain separately owned and operated.
When a larger, more powerful company outright buys a smaller company and absorbs it into its operations. The smaller company ceases to exist as an independent entity.
The concept that the combined value and performance of two companies will be greater than the sum of the separate individual parts. They merge to achieve 'Synergy'.

fun_activity.title: 🍔 Franchise Finder
fun_activity.instructions: Think about your local market or mall. Write down the names of 5 international or national brands that operate as Franchises (Hint: fast-food chains are a great place to start). Why do you think the local owner chose to buy a franchise instead of starting their own brand?

exam_tips: 📌 'Synergy' is frequently asked. Define it simply as the '2+2=5 effect' where combining creates extra value.
📌 Be ready to list the advantages of franchising from BOTH the Franchisor's perspective and the Franchisee's perspective.
📌 Distinguish between Mergers (friendly joining of equals) and Acquisitions (one buying out another, sometimes hostile).
quick_recap: ⭐ Franchising allows a company to expand rapidly without investing its own capital for each new location.
⭐ A horizontal merger happens between companies in the same industry (e.g., two banks merging).
⭐ External expansion strategies offer a faster route to growth and market dominance than internal expansion.
